title: In-silico identification of host-key-genes associated with dengue-virus-infections highlighting their pathogenetic mechanisms and therapeutic agents.
authors: Latif, Md Abdul; Noman, Md Al; Ahmmed, Reaz; Hossain, Md Sanoar; Ahmed, Md Foysal; Pappu, Md Al Amin; Islam, Md Shariful; Noor, Tasfia; Kabir, Md Hadiul; Mollah, Md Nurul Haque
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组差异表达与PPI网络识别登革热宿主关键基因，并做分子对接筛选药物，虽涉及转录因子调控网络，但核心是疾病基因与药物发现，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Dengue fever (DF), a potentially fatal mosquito-transmitted viral disease caused by dengue virus (DENV) infections (DENVI), stands as the predominant arthropod-borne viral illness worldwide, presenting a significant global health challenge. DENV-mediated proteins/proteases interact with host proteins to develop the infection. Despite the severity of DENVI, the infection-causing host key-genes (hKGs), their pathogenetic processes, and inhibitors/activators are not yet rigorously investigated. This study aimed to disclose DENVI-causing hKGs, highlighting their pathogenetic mechanisms and therapeutic agents. At first, 115 host differentially expressed genes (hDEGs) between DENVI and control samples were identified by employing the LIMMA statistical approach. Through protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, the top nine hDEGs (CDK1, BIRC5, TYMS, KIF20A, CCNB2, CDC20, AURKB, TK1, and PTEN) were detected as the infection-causing hGBs or host key-genes (hKGs). Among these hKGs, six genes (CDK1, BIRC5, TYMS, KIF20A, CCNB2, and TK1) have been emphasized as the DENVI-causing genes by the literature review. Functional enrichment analysis showed how hKGs orchestrate viral infection processes by disrupting cell cycles and immune responses. CDK1 and AURKB divert mitotic machinery to support viral replication, while PTEN and BIRC5 inhibit MAVS-MDA5 pathways to suppress interferon responses. In the nucleus, CDK1 and TYMS manipulate host transcription to favor viral processes. Key pathways identified through KEGG analysis include cell cycle and p53 signaling, explaining DENV-induced thrombocytopenia and dysregulated apoptosis. The regulatory network analysis identified five transcription factors (FOXC1, GATA2, RELA, TP53, PPARG) as the transcriptomic regulators of hKGs. The regulators FOXC1 and RELA influence EMT and inflammatory responses, and PPARG's involvement in lipid metabolism correlates with Dengue Shock Syndrome severity, while miR-103a-3p enhances viral replication by targeting the OTUD4/p38 MAPK pathway. Finally, hKGs-guided three drug candidates (ENTRECTINIB, IMATINIB, and QL47) were selected by molecular docking analysis. These findings provide valuable insights that could significantly impact dengue fever diagnosis and treatment strategies.
abstract_zh: 登革热（Dengue fever, DF）是一种由登革病毒（dengue virus, DENV）感染（DENVI）引起的潜在致命性蚊媒病毒性疾病，是全球最主要的节肢动物传播病毒性疾病，构成重大全球健康挑战。DENV介导的蛋白质/蛋白酶与宿主蛋白相互作用以发展感染。尽管DENVI严重，但引起感染的宿主关键基因（hKGs）、其致病过程及抑制剂/激活剂尚未得到严格研究。本研究旨在揭示导致DENVI的hKGs，突出其致病机制和治疗药物。首先，通过采用LIMMA统计方法，在DENVI与对照样本之间鉴定出115个宿主差异表达基因（hDEGs）。通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析，前九个hDEGs（CDK1、BIRC5、TYMS、KIF20A、CCNB2、CDC20、AURKB、TK1和PTEN）被检测为引起感染的宿主关键基因（hKGs）。在这些hKGs中，六个基因（CDK1、BIRC5、TYMS、KIF20A、CCNB2和TK1）经文献综述被强调为DENVI致病基因。功能富集分析显示hKGs如何通过破坏细胞周期和免疫反应来协调病毒感染过程。CDK1和AURKB将有丝分裂机制转向支持病毒复制，而PTEN和BIRC5抑制MAVS-MDA5通路以抑制干扰素反应。在细胞核中，CDK1和TYMS操纵宿主转录以利于病毒过程。通过KEGG分析鉴定的关键通路包括细胞周期和p53信号通路，解释了DENV诱导的血小板减少症和失调的细胞凋亡。调控网络分析鉴定出五个转录因子（FOXC1、GATA2、RELA、TP53、PPARG）作为hKGs的转录组调控因子。调控因子FOXC1和RELA影响上皮-间质转化（EMT）和炎症反应，PPARG在脂质代谢中的参与与登革休克综合征严重程度相关，而miR-103a-3p通过靶向OTUD4/p38 MAPK通路增强病毒复制。最后，通过分子对接分析选择了hKGs引导的三种候选药物（ENTRECTINIB、IMATINIB和QL47）。这些发现提供了有价值的见解，可能显著影响登革热的诊断和治疗策略。
